justification: The Housing SEPP eligibility route reported every form eligible once its zone matched and no lot row stopped it. A form with no lot standard in the dataset therefore passed by default: until 2026-09-15 that was manor_house, whose rows were really section 108 standards for independent living units, so users were told a Manor House was eligible, with a 'SEPP allows 9.5m vs LEP' override. The rows were relabelled in production on 2026-09-15; without this change the route would now say the same about independent living units.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A form with no lot standard in the dataset comes back isEligible true, or a SEPP-over-LEP override is listed for a form that was not found eligible.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Against the route on main, 2 of the 6 new tests failed: independent_living_unit came back eligible in R2, and the overrides for a lot outside a reform area listed independent_living_unit and residential_flat_r1r2. With the fix all 15 tests in the two eligibility suites pass.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Housing SEPP (in force 15 Sep 2026) section 108 is headed 'Non-discretionary development standards for independent living units' and states the 9.5m height, 0.5:1 FSR, landscaped area and 15% deep soil standards that the table had filed as manor house rules. No manor house minimum lot standard is in housing_sepp_standards.

pre_impl.existing_data: housing_sepp_standards: 45 rows across 8 forms after the 2026-09-15 correction. Only independent_living_unit (4 rows) has no min_lot_size among forms outside the base set and the station-distance apartment forms; dual_occupancy, multi_dwelling, residential_flat_r1r2, secondary_dwelling and terraces all have one.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The route assumed every form in the table carries a lot standard, so reaching the end of the checks meant eligible. services/housing_sepp_eligibility.py already treats a missing lot standard as not assessable; the two implementations disagreed.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Mirrors the existing Python guard (_BASE_FORMS and the residential_flat_r3r4 exemption) and the brief's eligible-only override rule. No new query, no change to the response shape; one display name and one page label added.

functions.name: POST
functions.input: zoneCode, lotSize, lotWidth, optional stationDistance, isLMRArea, lepHeight and lepFsr.
functions.output: One eligibility result per form applicable to the zone; a form outside the base set with no lot standard in the dataset is isEligible false with assessmentStatus 'not_assessed'; overrides only for forms found eligible.
functions.if_none: No standards rows returns no forms and no overrides; a failed read returns the existing 500 error.

values.if_missing: For a form outside the base set that is not a station-distance apartment form, the result is not assessed instead of eligible.
A form not found eligible gets no SEPP-over-LEP override line.

queries.purpose: Read every Housing SEPP standard with its form, zones, reform-area flag and clause to decide each form's eligibility.
queries.where_clause: FROM housing_sepp_standards ORDER BY development_type, standard_type (unchanged; all 45 standards are read and filtered by zones in code)

break_it.scenario: A form in the table has no lot standard in the dataset (independent living units since the 2026-09-15 relabel; manor houses before it).
break_it.what_happens: Every check is skipped and the form is reported eligible, with its Housing SEPP standard read as an entitlement for that form in any listed zone.
break_it.how: The route returns not assessed for such a form, as housing_sepp_eligibility.py does. test 'is not reported eligible, and says it was not assessed'; removing the guard failed 2 tests.

break_it.scenario: The guard also catches the base forms (secondary dwelling, dual occupancy) that are assessed without a lot standard.
break_it.what_happens: A granny flat would stop being reported eligible on any lot, a false negative on the most common question.
break_it.how: BASE_FORMS matches the Python set; dropping the exemption failed 'does not catch the base forms'.

break_it.scenario: The guard catches the station-distance apartment forms, which have no lot standard row but their own distance check.
break_it.what_happens: Mid-rise apartments near a station would never be reported eligible.
break_it.how: The residential_flat_r3r4 exemption is kept; removing it failed 'leaves the station-distance apartment forms to their own check'.

break_it.scenario: A SEPP-over-LEP height or FSR override is listed for a form the property cannot use or that was not assessed, in zones where the Housing SEPP standard exists.
break_it.what_happens: The response says the SEPP allows 9.5m over the LEP for that form, which reads as an entitlement the property does not have.
break_it.how: Overrides are built only for forms found eligible; removing the filter failed 'are listed only for forms found eligible'.

break_it.scenario: The unassessable form is reported as a confirmed negative instead of a check that did not run.
break_it.what_happens: A consumer reading assessmentStatus would tell the user the form is ineligible, a finding nobody made.
break_it.how: assessmentStatus is 'not_assessed'; changing it to 'ineligible' failed the first test.

mutation_analysis: Five mutations on route.ts, restored after, against the new suite and __tests__/api/housing-sepp-lmr-default.test.ts: guard removed -> 2 failed; base forms not exempt -> 1 failed; station-distance forms not exempt -> 1 failed; overrides for every form -> 1 failed; status 'ineligible' instead of 'not_assessed' -> 1 failed. Unmutated: 15 passed. The fixture takes its zones from HOUSING_SEPP_LMR.ELIGIBLE_ZONES, the route's own set, rather than a new literal list (zone-code lint).
residual_risk: The route is still a separate implementation of services/housing_sepp_eligibility.py (DQ-30 consolidation candidate), so a future change to one will not reach the other. The route still does not read stale_since, so a standard flagged stale by the law monitor is served here without the notice the Python engine carries. /api/tod/parking-rates still selects columns housing_sepp_standards does not have and reports its SEPP tier as degraded on every call; left as is because making it answer would present the conditional 0.5-space minimum in section 179(2)(c) as an overriding rate.

post_merge.db_reset: No reset. The data half was applied to production on 2026-09-15 by a guarded one-off script (backup data/db_rollback_backups/housing_sepp_standards_pre_correction_2026-09-15_2044.csv): 13 standards re-cited to today's Housing SEPP with the quoted text recorded, 4 relabelled manor_house -> independent_living_unit, 1 relabelled max_height -> setback_height_threshold; total unchanged at 45, none stale.
post_merge.manual_verify: POST /api/housing-sepp/eligibility with {"zoneCode":"R2","lotSize":600,"lotWidth":15,"isLMRArea":true} lists Independent Living Units as not assessed and no Manor House entry; /planning-standards shows 'Independent Living Units' with 4 standards.
